storyTitle: As an IT Manager, I want to view agent workload dashboards so that I can balance assignments across support agents

functional.title: Authorized IT Manager opens workload dashboard and sees queue and agent aggregates derived from latest valid assignment records
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated through enterprise SSO and has manager reporting permission for Team Alpha and its queues Queue-A and Queue-B.

Support ticket data exists in the authorized scope with latest valid assignment events as follows: TCK-2048 assigned to AGENT-12 in Queue-A, TCK-2055 reassigned from AGENT-12 to AGENT-17 in Queue-A, and T-1001 assigned to AGENT-12 in Queue-B.

Historical assignment records exist for TCK-2055 showing an older assignment to AGENT-12 and a newer valid assignment to AGENT-17 so current ownership can be validated against the latest valid assignment event.
The agent workload dashboard route and GET /api/dashboards/agent-workload endpoint are available in the test environment and audit history can be queried by authorized QA support.

steps.action: Sign in as MGR-04 through SSO and navigate to the "Agent Workload Dashboard" from the Support Operations Dashboard menu.
steps.expectedResult: Access is granted and the dashboard begins loading without any authorization error.

steps.action: Wait for the default dashboard summary to finish loading with no manual filters applied.
steps.expectedResult: The dashboard displays current assigned ticket counts grouped by queue and by current responsible support agent within MGR-04's authorized scope.

steps.action: Review the queue summary cards or rows for Queue-A and Queue-B.
steps.expectedResult: Queue-A shows 2 currently assigned tickets and Queue-B shows 1 currently assigned ticket, matching the current ownership test data.

steps.action: Review the agent summary section for AGENT-12 and AGENT-17.
steps.expectedResult: AGENT-12 shows 2 currently assigned tickets and AGENT-17 shows 1 currently assigned ticket; TCK-2055 is counted only under AGENT-17 and not under AGENT-12 because the latest valid assignment record determines current ownership.

steps.action: Cross-check one ticket with reassignment history by opening available tooltip, linked count details, or supporting row details for AGENT-17 if present.
steps.expectedResult: The dashboard representation of current ownership remains aligned to the latest valid assignment event and does not double-count the reassigned ticket in aggregate totals.

steps.action: Open the corresponding audit history entry for the dashboard view using authorized audit access or supporting test instrumentation.
steps.expectedResult: An audit record exists for the dashboard access with actor MGR-04, a current timestamp, the dashboard identifier, and the default filter context used for the view.

postconditions: No ticket ownership data is changed; the test is read-only against dashboard data.
A dashboard view audit history record exists for MGR-04 with timestamp and filter context.
MGR-04 remains logged in on the agent workload dashboard.

functional.title: Manager applies valid team, queue, category, and date range filters and receives consistent per-agent workload breakdown metrics from the filtered ticket set
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated through enterprise SSO and has manager reporting permission for Team Alpha, Queue-A, and Queue-B only.

Authorized dataset contains tickets in multiple categories and dates, including within scope records for Team Alpha: TCK-2048 category "Hardware" priority "High" status "Open" overdue yes created within the last 7 days, TCK-2055 category "Hardware" priority "Medium" status "In Progress" overdue no created within the last 7 days, and T-1001 category "Software" priority "Low" status "Open" overdue no created within the last 30 days.
At least one out-of-filter ticket exists in Team Alpha with category not equal to "Hardware" and at least one ticket exists outside MGR-04's authorized team to prove scope and filter behavior.
Dashboard summary and breakdown widgets display agent workload by priority, status, and overdue volume.

steps.action: Navigate to the loaded Agent Workload Dashboard as MGR-04.
steps.expectedResult: The default summary is visible and the filter controls for Team, Queue, Category, and Date Range are available.

steps.action: Set Team filter to "Team Alpha", Queue filter to "Queue-A", Category filter to "Hardware", and Date Range to the last 7 days, then click the "Apply Filters" button.
steps.expectedResult: The dashboard refreshes successfully using the selected filter set and remains within MGR-04's authorized reporting scope.

steps.action: Review the refreshed queue summary and total assigned ticket count.
steps.expectedResult: Only Queue-A hardware tickets within the selected date range are included; the summary total equals 2 and excludes T-1001 because it is in category "Software" and/or outside the selected queue.

steps.action: Review the per-agent workload breakdown cards or rows for AGENT-12 and AGENT-17.
steps.expectedResult: The filtered breakdown shows AGENT-12 with 1 ticket and AGENT-17 with 1 ticket, and the sum of agent counts equals the filtered queue total.

steps.action: Inspect the priority distribution, status distribution, and overdue count shown for the filtered result set.
steps.expectedResult: The workload breakdown reflects only the filtered tickets: one High priority and one Medium priority ticket, statuses matching the filtered records, and overdue count equal to 1 based on TCK-2048.

steps.action: Verify that no unauthorized team or queue data appears in totals, legends, or agent rows after filtering.
steps.expectedResult: Only data from Team Alpha and authorized queues is shown; no data from teams or queues outside MGR-04's scope is displayed.

steps.action: Open the corresponding audit history entry for this filtered dashboard view.
steps.expectedResult: An audit record is written for MGR-04 that includes the selected filter context: team, queue, category, and date range.

postconditions: The dashboard remains filtered to Team Alpha, Queue-A, Hardware, and the selected 7-day date range until changed or navigated away from.
Filtered summary and per-agent workload metrics are displayed using only authorized records in scope.
A dashboard view audit entry exists containing the applied filter context.

functional.title: Manager drills down from queue summary to agent detail and receives detail data consistent with the summary totals under the same filters
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated and authorized for Team Alpha and Queue-A.
The dashboard is loaded with an applied filter set of Team Alpha, Queue-A, Category "Hardware", and last 7 days, producing a summary total of 2 tickets split across AGENT-12 and AGENT-17.
The drill-down endpoint GET /api/dashboards/agent-workload/drilldown is available and returns assignment distribution data by selected queue or agent.
Audit history for drill-down events is enabled and queryable by authorized QA support.

steps.action: From the filtered Agent Workload Dashboard, note the Queue-A summary total and the agent summary counts currently displayed.
steps.expectedResult: Queue-A total is visible as 2 with AGENT-12 = 1 and AGENT-17 = 1 under the current filters.

steps.action: Click the Queue-A summary card or row to open the workload drill-down view.
steps.expectedResult: The drill-down page or panel opens and preserves the existing Team Alpha, Queue-A, Hardware, and date range filters.

steps.action: Review the assignment distribution data in the drill-down for agent-level details.
steps.expectedResult: The drill-down lists AGENT-12 and AGENT-17 with one ticket each, and the combined detail count equals the Queue-A summary total of 2.

steps.action: Select the AGENT-17 row or link within the drill-down to inspect ticket-level or agent-level assignment details.
steps.expectedResult: The system shows AGENT-17 detail for the same preserved filters and includes TCK-2055 as the currently assigned ticket.

steps.action: Compare the drill-down details for AGENT-17 with the summary-level count shown before drill-down.
steps.expectedResult: The AGENT-17 detail count matches the summary count of 1 and does not include tickets outside the applied filter set.

steps.action: Use the breadcrumb or back navigation to return to the previous workload summary view.
steps.expectedResult: The user returns to the summary dashboard with the same filters still applied and the same totals displayed.

steps.action: Review audit history for the drill-down action.
steps.expectedResult: An audit record exists for the drill-down access with actor MGR-04, timestamp, target queue or agent, and the preserved filter context.

postconditions: No operational ticket data is modified; only dashboard and drill-down views are accessed.
Applied filters remain preserved across drill-down and return navigation.
A drill-down audit history record exists with manager identity, timestamp, and filter context.

negative.title: Dashboard rejects invalid date range inputs and does not refresh workload results with malformed or reversed dates
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated through SSO and is authorized to access the Agent Workload Dashboard.
The dashboard is loaded successfully with a known baseline summary visible before invalid input testing begins.
Date range filter supports manual entry or picker selection for startDate and endDate and performs backend validation.

steps.action: Open the Agent Workload Dashboard and note the currently displayed summary totals and last successful filter state.
steps.expectedResult: A valid workload summary is visible and can be used as the baseline for confirming no unintended refresh occurs.

steps.action: In the Date Range filter, enter a malformed start date such as "2025-13-40" and a valid end date such as "2025-01-31", then click "Apply Filters".
steps.expectedResult: The system rejects the request, highlights the date input as invalid, and shows a clear validation error indicating the date format is invalid; the dashboard data does not refresh.

steps.action: Correct the malformed value, then enter Start Date "2025-02-15" and End Date "2025-02-01", and click "Apply Filters" again.
steps.expectedResult: The system rejects the date range because end date is earlier than start date, presents an error message explaining the range is invalid, and keeps the prior valid summary data unchanged.

steps.action: Review queue totals, agent totals, and any loading indicators after each invalid submission.
steps.expectedResult: No new summary or drill-down data is loaded from the invalid requests; the last valid dataset remains displayed without partial refresh or inconsistent counts.

steps.action: If network inspection or API logs are available, review the response for the invalid submissions.
steps.expectedResult: The backend validation rejects the invalid filter input and returns a client error response rather than processing unauthorized or malformed query data.

steps.action: Check audit history or structured logs for the attempted invalid filter actions if available to QA.
steps.expectedResult: The system records the dashboard access context without exposing sensitive data; invalid filter attempts do not create misleading successful view records for refreshed data.

postconditions: The dashboard remains on the last successfully loaded summary state.
No filtered dataset is saved or shown for the invalid date submissions.
Validation errors are presented to the user and invalid query data is not processed into workload calculations.

negative.title: User without required manager reporting permission is denied access to dashboard and drill-down endpoints and the attempt is audit logged
preconditions: User AGENT-12 is authenticated through enterprise SSO but does not have manager reporting permission for the workload dashboard.
The agent workload dashboard route and drill-down endpoint are deployed and protected by RBAC and reporting scope enforcement.
Audit history captures denied access attempts with actor identity, timestamp, and requested resource context.

steps.action: Sign in as AGENT-12 and navigate directly to the Agent Workload Dashboard URL or menu route.
steps.expectedResult: Access is denied; the dashboard data is not displayed and the user sees an authorization error or access denied state.

steps.action: Confirm that no queue summaries, agent counts, overdue counts, or other restricted workload details are rendered on the page.
steps.expectedResult: No restricted dashboard content is exposed to AGENT-12.

steps.action: Using the same session, call or navigate directly to a drill-down request for Queue-A, for example the route or request equivalent of GET /api/dashboards/agent-workload/drilldown?queueId=Queue-A.
steps.expectedResult: The system denies the drill-down request as well and returns an authorization failure without exposing assignment distribution details.

steps.action: Inspect the UI response and, if available, the network response status for both denied requests.
steps.expectedResult: Both requests fail with a permission-related response and do not fall back to generic success or partial data states.

steps.action: Review audit history for AGENT-12's denied access attempts.
steps.expectedResult: Audit entries exist for the denied dashboard and denied drill-down access attempts, each capturing actor identity, timestamp, attempted resource, and denied outcome.

postconditions: AGENT-12 remains authenticated but cannot access manager-only dashboard or drill-down data.
No restricted workload information is disclosed in UI or API responses.
Denied access attempts are recorded in audit history with the correct outcome.

negative.title: Authorized manager is blocked from using out-of-scope team or queue filter values and no unauthorized data is returned
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated and has reporting permission only for Team Alpha with queues Queue-A and Queue-B.
A separate Team Beta and Queue-C exist in the system with active support tickets not included in MGR-04's reporting scope.
The dashboard supports filter inputs for teamId and queueId and validates scope on the backend.

steps.action: Open the Agent Workload Dashboard as MGR-04 and confirm the initial authorized summary loads successfully.
steps.expectedResult: Authorized data for Team Alpha appears with no errors.

steps.action: Attempt to filter the dashboard to an out-of-scope team by selecting or forcing Team Beta in the Team filter and clicking "Apply Filters".
steps.expectedResult: The system rejects the request because Team Beta is outside the manager's authorized reporting scope and does not display Team Beta data.

steps.action: Attempt to request an out-of-scope queue directly by using Queue-C in the filter or manipulating the request query for queueId=Queue-C.
steps.expectedResult: The system rejects the request through backend scope validation and returns no unauthorized queue summary, agent metrics, or drill-down data.

steps.action: Review the page state after each rejected scope violation attempt.
steps.expectedResult: The last valid authorized dashboard view remains intact, and the UI presents a clear authorization or scope validation message rather than mixing unauthorized and authorized results.

steps.action: Check audit history for MGR-04 after the out-of-scope attempts.
steps.expectedResult: The denied out-of-scope filter or endpoint requests are captured in audit history with MGR-04's identity, timestamp, attempted scope values, and denied outcome.

postconditions: The dashboard continues to show only authorized Team Alpha data.
No Team Beta or Queue-C data is returned or visible to MGR-04.
Out-of-scope access attempts are audit logged as denied.

edgeCases.title: Dashboard returns zero-result summaries and empty drill-down cleanly when valid filters produce no matching tickets within manager scope
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated through SSO and has manager reporting permission for Team A and Queue Q-HELP only.
There are active tickets in Team A and Queue Q-HELP, but no tickets in category 'Hardware Refresh' with assignment dates between 2030-01-01 and 2030-01-31.
The agent workload dashboard and drill-down endpoints are available in the test environment.
Audit history is queryable for dashboard view and drill-down events for user MGR-04.

steps.action: Open the Agent Workload Dashboard as MGR-04.
steps.expectedResult: The dashboard loads successfully and displays default workload summary cards grouped by queue and current responsible support agent for the manager's authorized scope.

steps.action: Set filters to Team = 'Team A', Queue = 'Q-HELP', Category = 'Hardware Refresh', Start Date = '2030-01-01', End Date = '2030-01-31', then click 'Apply Filters'.
steps.expectedResult: The system accepts the filter values as syntactically valid and refreshes the dashboard using only the filtered dataset within authorized scope.

steps.action: Review the queue summary cards, agent summary area, and per-agent workload breakdown sections after refresh.
steps.expectedResult: The dashboard shows a valid empty-state presentation with zero assigned ticket counts, zero overdue counts, and no misleading residual data from the previous view.

steps.action: Select any available queue summary card or use the queue drill-down action from the empty filtered state if the UI exposes it.
steps.expectedResult: The drill-down opens with the same preserved filters and displays no matching assignment distribution records rather than an error or unauthorized message.

steps.action: Verify the drill-down totals for ticket count, overdue count, and any status or priority breakdown values.
steps.expectedResult: All drill-down totals remain 0 and are consistent with the summary totals for the same filters.

steps.action: Open audit history and locate the most recent dashboard access entries for MGR-04.
steps.expectedResult: Audit history contains entries for the dashboard view and the drill-down access, including manager identity, timestamp, and the applied filter context with Team A, Q-HELP, Hardware Refresh, 2030-01-01, and 2030-01-31.

postconditions: No dashboard or assignment data is modified.
The filtered empty-state view remains accessible to MGR-04 with preserved filter values.
Audit history contains immutable records for the zero-result dashboard view and drill-down access.

edgeCases.title: Dashboard uses the latest valid assignment event when reassignment history exists and keeps summary-to-drill-down totals consistent
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated through SSO and has manager reporting permission for Team A and Queue Q-HELP.

Test ticket TCK-2048 exists in Queue Q-HELP with assignment history showing AGENT-12 assigned first, then a later valid reassignment to AGENT-17; the current responsible agent in source data is AGENT-17.
At least one additional ticket assigned to AGENT-17 exists so workload totals are not singular, and priority, status, and overdue attributes are populated for the filtered date range.
Audit history is queryable for dashboard and drill-down events generated during the test.

steps.action: Open the Agent Workload Dashboard as MGR-04.
steps.expectedResult: The dashboard loads successfully for the manager's authorized scope.

steps.action: Apply filters Team = 'Team A', Queue = 'Q-HELP', Start Date = a range covering both the original assignment and later reassignment events for TCK-2048, and leave Category unfiltered.
steps.expectedResult: The dashboard refreshes and recalculates summary counts using the filtered dataset and current responsible agent logic.

steps.action: Inspect the agent summary rows for AGENT-12 and AGENT-17 and note the assigned ticket totals.
steps.expectedResult: TCK-2048 contributes to AGENT-17's current assigned ticket count and does not appear counted under AGENT-12 as current ownership.

steps.action: Review AGENT-17's workload breakdown on the dashboard for priority distribution, status distribution, and overdue volume.
steps.expectedResult: The breakdown includes TCK-2048 in the correct priority, status, and overdue grouping derived from the filtered ticket set.

steps.action: Click AGENT-17 or the related queue summary to open drill-down details while keeping the same filters.
steps.expectedResult: The drill-down opens with preserved filters and displays detailed assignment distribution for AGENT-17.

steps.action: Locate TCK-2048 in the drill-down details and compare the drill-down totals with the parent summary totals.
steps.expectedResult: TCK-2048 appears under AGENT-17 in drill-down results, and the drill-down ticket count, overdue count, and related distribution totals are consistent with the corresponding dashboard summary values.

steps.action: Open audit history for MGR-04 after the drill-down.
steps.expectedResult: Audit history records both the dashboard view and drill-down access with manager identity, timestamp, and the applied filter context.

postconditions: No ticket assignments are changed by viewing the dashboard.
Summary and drill-down evidence confirms current ownership is derived from the latest valid assignment event for TCK-2048.
Audit history contains immutable records of the dashboard and drill-down access.

edgeCases.title: Dashboard honors a boundary date range where start date equals end date and includes only records for that single day
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated through SSO and has manager reporting permission for Team A and Queue Q-HELP.
For date '2026-06-15', Queue Q-HELP contains at least two tickets assigned to current agents within Team A, and there are additional tickets on '2026-06-14' and '2026-06-16' that should be excluded.
Ticket priority, status, and overdue values are available for the 2026-06-15 records.
The dashboard supports Start Date and End Date filter fields.

steps.action: Open the Agent Workload Dashboard as MGR-04.
steps.expectedResult: The dashboard loads the default summary view for the authorized scope.

steps.action: Set Team = 'Team A', Queue = 'Q-HELP', Start Date = '2026-06-15', End Date = '2026-06-15', then click 'Apply Filters'.
steps.expectedResult: The system accepts the date range because the end date is not earlier than the start date and refreshes the dashboard.

steps.action: Review the queue and agent summary totals after the refresh.
steps.expectedResult: Only records falling on 2026-06-15 are included in assigned ticket counts; records from 2026-06-14 and 2026-06-16 are excluded.

steps.action: Verify one agent's breakdown for priority distribution, status distribution, and overdue count against the known 2026-06-15 dataset.
steps.expectedResult: The displayed breakdown values reflect only the single-day filtered records and match expected counts for that date.

steps.action: Open queue or agent drill-down from the filtered summary.
steps.expectedResult: The drill-down preserves the same single-day date range and returns details only for 2026-06-15.

steps.action: Compare the drill-down totals with the summary totals for the same filters.
steps.expectedResult: The drill-down totals match the summary totals exactly for the single-day range.

postconditions: The dashboard remains filtered to the single-day range 2026-06-15.
No data is updated or removed.
Summary and drill-down results confirm correct handling of the start-date-equals-end-date boundary.

accessibility.title: Keyboard-only user can open the dashboard, apply filters, and reach drill-down without losing focus context
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated through SSO and has manager reporting permission for Team A and Queue Q-HELP.
The Agent Workload Dashboard contains visible filter controls for Team, Queue, Category, Start Date, End Date, an 'Apply Filters' action, and at least one queue or agent drill-down target.
Test is executed on a desktop browser with a keyboard only; mouse input is not used.
A visible focus indicator is enabled in the browser and not suppressed by custom styling.

steps.action: Open the Agent Workload Dashboard and press Tab from the browser content area through the page header into the first interactive dashboard element.
steps.expectedResult: Keyboard focus moves in a logical order to the first actionable control on the dashboard, and the focused element is clearly visible.

steps.action: Use Tab, Shift+Tab, arrow keys, and Enter/Space as applicable to navigate and set Team = 'Team A' and Queue = 'Q-HELP' without using a mouse.
steps.expectedResult: Dropdowns and selectors are operable by keyboard, announce or visually show the currently selected option, and do not trap focus.

steps.action: Continue by keyboard to the Start Date and End Date fields, enter a valid date range, and activate the 'Apply Filters' button with Enter or Space.
steps.expectedResult: The filter action executes successfully from the keyboard, and focus remains on the filter action or is moved predictably to the refreshed results region without jumping to the top of the page.

steps.action: After the dashboard refresh, Tab to a queue summary card or agent row that supports drill-down and activate it using Enter.
steps.expectedResult: The drill-down opens successfully from keyboard interaction alone, preserving the applied filters.

steps.action: In the drill-down view, continue tabbing through the detail content and then use the provided breadcrumb or Back control to return to the dashboard.
steps.expectedResult: All interactive elements in the drill-down are keyboard reachable, the return control is keyboard operable, and the user returns to the dashboard with prior filters preserved.

steps.action: Observe focus location after returning from drill-down.
steps.expectedResult: Focus lands on a meaningful element such as the originating summary item, drill-down heading, or breadcrumb/back control rather than being lost or reset unpredictably.

postconditions: No data is modified by the keyboard-only interaction.
The dashboard remains usable without mouse input for the core workflow of filtering and drill-down.
Applied filters remain preserved after drill-down and return navigation.

accessibility.title: Screen reader exposes dashboard structure, filter controls, summaries, and error messaging with meaningful labels and updates
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated through SSO and has manager reporting permission for the dashboard.
A screen reader such as NVDA or JAWS is running on a supported desktop browser.
The dashboard includes a page title, labeled filter fields, summary cards or agent rows, and validation messaging for invalid date ranges.
At least one valid summary result is available before inducing an invalid filter.

steps.action: Open the Agent Workload Dashboard with the screen reader enabled and listen to the initial page announcement.
steps.expectedResult: The page announces a meaningful title such as Agent Workload Dashboard and exposes landmark or heading structure that helps the user identify the main content region.

steps.action: Navigate to the filter area using screen reader landmark, heading, or form navigation commands.
steps.expectedResult: Filter controls are discoverable and each field is announced with a clear accessible name, such as Team, Queue, Category, Start Date, and End Date.

steps.action: Read the summary content using table, list, or grouped element navigation on the loaded dashboard.
steps.expectedResult: Queue and agent workload summaries are announced with enough context to identify the entity and count values, rather than unlabeled numbers or generic clickable items.

steps.action: Enter an invalid date range using the filter controls, for example Start Date = '2026-06-20' and End Date = '2026-06-10', then activate 'Apply Filters'.
steps.expectedResult: The system rejects the invalid range and the error is announced by the screen reader with clear text indicating the end date cannot be earlier than the start date.

steps.action: Move focus back through the Start Date and End Date fields after the validation error appears.
steps.expectedResult: The erroneous fields are programmatically associated with the validation message or invalid state so the screen reader identifies them as invalid and communicates the issue.

steps.action: Correct the filter to a valid range and apply it again, then open a drill-down item using screen reader navigation and keyboard activation.
steps.expectedResult: The refreshed results or drill-down heading is announced, demonstrating that state changes are communicated meaningfully after applying filters and opening details.

postconditions: No data is modified beyond reading and filtering dashboard content.
The dashboard remains accessible to screen reader users for the core flow of review, filter validation, and drill-down access.
Invalid date-range feedback is exposed through programmatic labels or announcements.

accessibility.title: Dashboard remains readable and actionable at 200% zoom with clear contrast for workload and overdue indicators
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated through SSO and has access to the Agent Workload Dashboard.
The dashboard contains queue summaries, agent rows, overdue indicators, priority or status breakdown labels, filter controls, and at least one drill-down target.
Browser zoom can be set to 200% on a 1440px desktop viewport or equivalent responsive desktop layout.
The environment allows visual inspection of text, icons, badges, and focus states.

steps.action: Open the Agent Workload Dashboard and set browser zoom to 200%.
steps.expectedResult: The page content enlarges without becoming unusable; core dashboard content remains present and no essential information disappears.

steps.action: Inspect the page title, filter labels, queue summary cards, agent workload rows, and overdue count indicators at 200% zoom.
steps.expectedResult: Text remains readable, labels do not overlap or truncate critical values, and information can be understood without relying on color alone.

steps.action: Check the visual presentation of overdue, priority, and status indicators, including any colored badges, charts, or labels.
steps.expectedResult: Indicators have sufficient foreground/background contrast and also include textual labels or counts so meaning is not conveyed by color alone.

steps.action: At 200% zoom, interact with Team, Queue, Start Date, End Date, and 'Apply Filters', then trigger a drill-down on a queue or agent.
steps.expectedResult: Controls remain visible and operable without horizontal-only dependency, and the user can still complete filtering and drill-down tasks.

steps.action: Observe the layout after drill-down opens and when returning to the main dashboard.
steps.expectedResult: Content reflows or remains navigable without clipping critical controls, and the preserved filters and summary information are still readable.

postconditions: The dashboard can still be used at 200% zoom for filter and drill-down workflows.
No data is changed as a result of zoom or display inspection.
Visual indicators for workload, overdue, priority, and status remain understandable and sufficiently distinguishable.

performance.title: Validate dashboard summary API performance under normal concurrent manager load
performance.description: Verify that GET /api/dashboards/agent-workload meets summary response time targets under expected business load with authorized IT Managers accessing default dashboard summaries concurrently. Measure P50, P95, P99 latency, TPS, error rate, and infrastructure utilization while validating the 3-second target for standard filter combinations.
preconditions: Performance environment mirrors production topology, data volumes, indexes, and RBAC configuration
SSO authentication and manager role authorization are enabled
SupportTicket, Assignment, TicketStatusHistory, SLA Metric, Workload Metric, Dashboard, and Audit History stores are populated with realistic large assignment datasets
At least 100 active queues, 1000 agents, and 500000 tickets exist with current responsible agent derived from latest valid assignment events
Monitoring is enabled for API latency, TPS, CPU, memory, DB utilization, and error rates

steps.action: Configure a load test with 100 concurrent authenticated IT Manager virtual users calling GET /api/dashboards/agent-workload using default dashboard parameters within authorized scope.
steps.expectedResult: Traffic is generated successfully with all users authorized and workload distributed evenly across the test duration.

steps.action: Run the test for 30 minutes with a 5-minute ramp-up and steady-state period while capturing response time percentiles, TPS, error rate, CPU, memory, and database metrics.
steps.expectedResult: System remains stable for the full duration and produces complete telemetry for latency, throughput, resource usage, and failures.

steps.action: Analyze summary API performance against service targets.
steps.expectedResult: P50 response time is less than or equal to 1.5 seconds, P95 is less than or equal to 3 seconds, P99 is less than or equal to 4 seconds, error rate is less than 1%, and CPU and memory remain within agreed operational thresholds such as CPU below 70% average and memory below 75% average.

steps.action: Verify throughput and audit logging behavior during the same run.
steps.expectedResult: TPS remains consistent without backlog buildup and dashboard view audit events are recorded asynchronously without causing material latency increase.

postconditions: Performance results are stored and baseline thresholds documented
Audit logs generated during the run are retained for verification
Environment health is confirmed after the test
performance.testData: 100 manager users such as MGR-04 to MGR-103, default authorized scope, active queues, large ticket ownership dataset with overdue and high-priority tickets

performance.title: Validate filtered dashboard summary performance across common filter combinations
performance.description: Verify dashboard summary performance when managers apply team, queue, category, and date range filters concurrently. Confirm that filtered calculations remain performant and consistent under normal load for standard business usage patterns.
preconditions: Performance environment contains realistic team, queue, category, and date-range distributions
Query parameter validation is enabled
Authorized manager accounts exist with varied reporting scopes

steps.action: Create a mixed workload profile where 150 concurrent managers call GET /api/dashboards/agent-workload using a blend of standard filter combinations for teamId, queueId, categoryId, startDate, and endDate.
steps.expectedResult: Requests reflect realistic usage distribution across common filter combinations and remain within authorized scope.

steps.action: Execute the test for 45 minutes with a 10-minute ramp-up and maintain steady traffic.
steps.expectedResult: System processes filtered queries continuously without instability or noticeable latency drift.

steps.action: Measure response time percentiles, TPS, error rate, cache efficiency if applicable, and resource utilization across API and database layers.
steps.expectedResult: P50 is less than or equal to 2 seconds, P95 is less than or equal to 3 seconds, P99 is less than or equal to 5 seconds, error rate is less than 1%, and no resource bottleneck exceeds operational thresholds.

steps.action: Compare results across broad date ranges versus narrow date ranges and across high-cardinality queues or categories.
steps.expectedResult: Performance remains within acceptable variance and no specific filter dimension causes significant service degradation for standard use.

postconditions: Filter-specific latency baselines are documented
Slowest filter combinations are identified for optimization if needed
performance.testData: Mixed filters including teamId values for 20 teams, queueId values for 100 queues, categoryId values for 30 categories, and date ranges from 1 day to 90 days

performance.title: Validate drill-down API performance under normal concurrent usage
performance.description: Verify GET /api/dashboards/agent-workload/drilldown response times for queue and agent-level drill-down requests under concurrent manager usage with preserved filter context. Confirm the 5-second drill-down target for large assignment datasets.
preconditions: Large assignment datasets with dense assignment history are available

userStoryObject.title: As an IT Manager, I want to view agent workload dashboards so that I can balance assignments across support agents
userStoryObject.description:
CONTEXT & BACKGROUND:

The agent workload dashboard is needed within Support Operations Dashboard capabilities so IT Managers can compare assignment distribution across support agents and queues using live ticket ownership and assignment history. The story supports day-to-day queue management, reassignment oversight, and capacity decisions in the IT Help Desk Management System.

CURRENT STATE:

Managers must infer workload by checking multiple ticket lists, assignment changes, and status screens separately. This fragmented view makes it hard to see who currently owns work, which agents carry overdue or high-priority tickets, and whether recent reassignments have shifted workload unevenly.

DESIRED STATE:

An authorized IT Manager can open a single dashboard that summarizes current assigned ticket counts by queue and agent, apply filters for team, queue, category, and date range, and drill into agent-level detail without losing calculation consistency. Dashboard access is restricted by role and reporting scope and every view is audit logged.

KEY FUNCTIONALITY:

• Show current assigned ticket counts grouped by queue and current responsible support agent

• Break down each agent workload by ticket priority, status, and overdue volume

• Apply filters for team, queue, ticket category, and date range with backend scope validation

• Provide drill-down from queue summary cards to agent-level ticket distribution details

• Record dashboard view activity in audit history with manager identity, timestamp, and filter context


USER INTERACTION FLOW:

1. The IT Manager authenticates through enterprise sign-in and opens the agent workload dashboard.

2. The system validates the user has manager reporting permission for the selected organizational scope.

3. The dashboard loads default workload summaries by queue and by current assigned agent.

4. The IT Manager applies filters for team, queue, category, and date range.

5. The system refreshes charts, totals, and overdue counts using the same workload rules.

6. The IT Manager selects a queue or agent row to open drill-down details.

7. The system displays agent-level assignment distribution and writes an audit entry for the dashboard access.


TECHNICAL CONSIDERATIONS:

• Data comes from SupportTicket, Assignment, TicketStatusHistory, SLA Metric, Workload Metric, Dashboard, and Audit History stores, with current responsible agent derived from latest valid assignment event

• Filter validation must reject malformed dates, end dates earlier than start dates, unsupported aggregation levels, and queue or team values outside the manager's authorized scope

• API support should cover GET /api/dashboards/agent-workload and GET /api/dashboards/agent-workload/drilldown with query fields such as teamId, queueId, categoryId, startDate, endDate, and agentId

• Access requires SSO-authenticated manager roles, RBAC scope enforcement, sanitized query parameters, and audit logging of view and drill-down activity

• Summary responses should return within 3 seconds and drill-down responses within 5 seconds for large assignment datasets, with structured logs and metrics for latency and authorization failures


OUT OF SCOPE:

• Automatically redistributing tickets based on dashboard results

• Calculating employee performance scores or quality ratings

• Workforce planning outside help desk queues and support teams


SUCCESS METRICS:

• All active support queues visible to a manager's scope appear in dashboard summaries

• Summary dashboard queries meet a 3 second response target for standard filter combinations

• All workload dashboard views and drill-down accesses are captured in audit history

Persona: IT Manager (IT Manager)

Design Prompt 

Unified interaction flow:
A ticket or SLA event occurs in the IT Help Desk system, such as ticket creation, assignment or reassignment, status update, comment, resolution, closure, SLA warning, SLA breach, escalation, or notification/reporting access.
The core ticket action is committed first, then a normalized notification or telemetry event is generated asynchronously so ticket processing is never blocked.
The notification orchestration layer evaluates event eligibility, recipient scope, role authorization, channel routing, sanitization, deduplication, and retry policy.
Employees receive only employee-safe lifecycle messages through confirmation, My Tickets, ticket detail, and status history touchpoints; agents receive operational assignment and activity signals; managers receive SLA risk and governance oversight signals; administrators and analysts access secure configuration, monitoring, and audit workflows.
Delivery outcomes such as SENT, FAILED, RETRIED, DENIED, and related states are recorded in immutable audit and telemetry history.
If access is unauthorized or delivery/configuration fails, the system preserves the committed source event, shows the correct denied or error state, and avoids leaking restricted ticket data, internal notes, attachment metadata, or secrets.

Figma Make instructions:

Create a web app system design for an IT Help Desk Management System focused only on notification-related experiences and the ticket lifecycle touchpoints that shape them.

Use a clean enterprise SaaS style:
- 1440px desktop frames
- neutral background
- blue primary actions
- semantic status colors
- compact data-dense layouts for ops/admin pages
- accessible spacing and strong hierarchy
- realistic top nav and left sidebar patterns

Global rules:
- Do not create any visible “User Journey” section in the UI
- Requester-facing screens must be sanitized and employee-safe
- Never expose internal comments, hidden notes, reassignment rationale for staff only, attachment internals, raw secrets, or restricted troubleshooting details on employee screens
- Monitoring and audit views are read-only unless the screen is explicitly configuration-related
- Show immutable audit concepts through labels, event history, timestamps, and references, not edit controls
- Unauthorized route states must be visually distinct from generic server errors
- Retry actions issue one new request and disable while in progress
- Preserve filters across drill-down, pagination, and return navigation on manager and ops screens

Create these pages:

Page 1: End User Notification Experiences
Build these frames:
1. Employee My Tickets
- top navigation with app name, notifications icon, profile menu
- lightweight left sidebar with My Tickets and New Ticket
- page title “My Tickets”
- filter chips for Status, Priority, Date Range
- table with columns: Ticket ID, Subject, Category, Priority, Current Status, Last Update, Notification Cue
- rows like TCK-2048, TCK-2055, T-1001
- show small status cues and safe notification indicators such as “Status updated”, “Resolved”, “Assigned”
- include pagination

2. Employee Ticket Detail
- breadcrumbs: My Tickets / TCK-2048
- ticket summary card with ticketId, category, priority, current status
- employee-safe timeline/history showing created, assigned, status updated, resolved, closed
- safe notification summary module with message preview cards for TICKET_CREATED, TICKET_ASSIGNED, TICKET_UPDATED, TICKET_RESOLVED, TICKET_CLOSED
- no internal agent notes
- include current status and timestamp labels

3. Ticket Created Success / Confirmation
- success panel with ticket reference, initial status, category, priority, created timestamp
- confirmation text that notification has been sent or queued
- CTA buttons: View Ticket, Back to My Tickets
- success toast variant visible

4. Unauthorized Ticket Access
- full-page access denied panel
- generic message without ticket details
- CTA: Return to My Tickets

5. No Tickets Empty State
- empty state panel with illustration placeholder
- text: “You have no support tickets yet”
- CTA: Create Ticket

Also include small state variants on this page:
- loading skeleton for My Tickets list
- validation error summary for invalid ticket lookup
- safe server error banner

Page 2: Agent and Manager Operational Notification Views
Build these frames:
1. Agent Ticket List
- top nav and left sidebar for agent workspace
- page title “Assigned Tickets”
- filter bar: Queue, Status, Priority, SLA State, Date Range
- table columns: Ticket ID, Subject, Assignee, Priority, Status, SLA State, Activity Indicator, Last Notification
- include assignment/activity icons for assignment, reassignment, comment, status change
- show denied-access row state pattern separately, not mixed with valid data
- include pagination

2. Agent Ticket Detail
- breadcrumbs: Assigned Tickets / TCK-2055
- header with ticket summary and assignment badge
- operational activity stream with assignment changes, comments, status changes, and notification states
- assignment history panel
- agent-targeted notification patterns for assignment, reassignment, comments, and status changes
- include visible status badges for Sent, Failed, Retried where notification outcomes are relevant
- include a denied-access state variant for out-of-scope ticket direct route

3. Reassignment Modal
- modal over agent detail
- assignee selector limited to eligible users only
- queue option if applicable
- inline eligibility validation
- confirm and cancel actions
- validation state if selected assignee is inactive or unauthorized
- disabled confirm while saving

4. Manager SLA / Notification Overview Dashboard
- KPI cards: At Risk, Breached, Overdue, Escalated, Active Notifications, Failed Deliveries
- cards for assignment/workload summaries
- SLA alert center list for approaching breach, breach, escalation
- visual labels for On Track, At Risk, Breached, Overdue
- filters: date range, category, priority, queue, team, agent
- governance evidence panel with audit summary snippets
- data currency label: “Last refreshed 09:42 AM”

5. Queue / Team / Agent Drill-down
- three adjacent or sequential frames showing preserved-filter drill-down:
  - Queue-level
  - Team-level
  - Agent-level
- each view shows ticket count, average aging, overdue count, SLA within target vs breached
- preserve filter chips and breadcrumbs back path
- include empty state and access denied variant for unauthorized drill-down

Page 3: Notification Administration and Integration Configuration
Build these frames:
1. Notification Rules List
- admin nav and left sidebar
- page title “Notification Rules”
- rule cards or table with trigger, recipient roles, timing, channel mapping, status
- actions: Create Rule, Edit, Activate, Deactivate
- audit reference visible on rows/cards
- governance banner at top

2. Rule Create / Edit Form
- form sections: Rule Name, Trigger Event, Recipient Roles, Timing, Active Status, Channel Mapping
- event options include TICKET_CREATED, TICKET_ASSIGNED, TICKET_UPDATED, TICKET_RESOLVED, TICKET_CLOSED, SLA_WARNING, SLA_BREACH, ESCALATION
- validation error summary at top
- inline field errors
- success state with audit reference after save
